recipes.name: Holland Cream (White Cream Filling)
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon water, or more as needed

steps.text: Stir sugar and 1/2 cup water together in a saucepan over medium heat until sugar has dissolved and mixture comes to a boil. Remove from the heat and let cool completely, 15 to 30 minutes.
Pour cooled syrup into a large mixing bowl. Add shortening, oil, and vanilla; beat with an electric mixer on high speed until well blended.
Beat in confectioners' sugar, 1 cup at a time, until filling is thick and fluffy.
Mix in water, 1 tablespoon at a time, if filling is too thick.

raw_recipe.headline: Holland Cream (White Cream Filling)
raw_recipe.description: Make tasty cream-filled donuts at home, similar to the ones you'd find in bakeries and pastry shops, with this sweet and fluffy white cream filling.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was really good and easy to make, I followed it excactly and it came out good. The second time I made it, I did change it a bit. Instead of two cups of shortening I used 1 cup of butter and 1 cup of shortening. It was wonderful.

Conversions 
(I use King Arthur's chart for each ingredient, not a 1 oz = 28g straight conversion. Even different type flours have a different weight per cup, it makes that much difference)

198 g sugar
111 g water
198 g veg oil
368 g veg shortening
4 g clear vanilla (typical 11 lb will not measure this low)
908 g confect sugar

I did the 1/2 butter 1/2 shortening recommended by many others, and liked the flavor. It is definitely a filling type icing, think the inside of a Hostess cupcake or a cream filled Krispy Kreme. It is super sweet and whips up light and creamy. 
I kept it on high in the stand mixer for 10 minutes, I think this is necessary for that airy texture. It was a little loose but good to pipe inside the cupcakes. Out of the fridge the next day, after about 10 minutes on the counter, it was a little firmer but didn't have to go back to the mixer.

I used it inside a chocolate cupcake with an unsweetened 60% chocolate ganache poured over. It needed the bitterness from the ganache to cut all of the sweet. Excellent together, all ages enjoyed.

I had some left over cream and mixed it with lemon curd (about 2 parts cream, 1 part thick curd) and used that to top a little 6" single chocolate layer cake. Good stuff.

A half recipe yielded about 4 cups. Makes a LOT.

This is a great base filling that my customers rave about. I am a professional baker and when I make this, I use no oil, just use a high ratio shortening and butter mix, and a little more vanilla. Make sure you sift your confection sugar and that your syrup is completely cooled and it won't be grainy. It will be delish! I pipe this into Cream Horns and Chocolate cupcakes.

It's fantastic but I admit my laziness probably saved me. Instead of 1/2 cup water and 1 cup sugar I used 3/4 cup simple syrup (from the mixed drinks aisle) and I tasted after the first heaping cup of powdered sugar. I ended up putting just under 2 cups in, and it was definitely sweet enough. No gritty texture, whipped up quick and delicious. Put it in a pastry bag and filled cupcakes.

This cream recipe is exactly what I've been looking for for many years! I did halve it. I used it for the filling in my pumpkin whoopie pies and it tasted just like the Amish one's in Shipshewana:)! I did do something different though. I didn't boil the sugar and water. I nuked it in the microwave for a minute until it was clear and then put it in the freezer for a couple of minutes to cool. You have to use CRISCO or it will taste really gross. Eating it alone, you will have a slight shortening taste. When eating it in the whoopie pie, you can't taste anything but pure bliss:D! My kids LOVED it!

I made 1/4 of the recipe for 12 chocolate cupcakes. I did use 1/2 butter and 1/2 shortening, and regular vanilla. I'm in an RV so supplies were limited. I used 1/2 filling, then converted the rest to chocolate frosting. Adding 3-4T Hershey chocolate syrup (all I had for chocolate), 1&3/4C powder sugar, and 2-3t milk. They turned out awesome, and filling is perfect.

This was exactly what I wanted for a cupcake filling. Adjusted the recipe down to a manageable 25 cupcakes portion and followed the recipe exactly. Light and fluffy and sweet enough to balance the cake. I turned half of it into a raspberry cream filling by macerating frozen raspberries and adding the juice to the filling. Bright pink in color but a wonderful raspberry flavor that balanced the lemon frosting and white cake.
It is amazing. Exactly like the KK donut filling thank you so much. I 1/4 the recipe for a cupcake filling and 2 days later doubled that for frosting on cupcakes.
I tried it for the first time today and I did as some of the others did and used 1 cup of butter and 1 cup of shortening and this has got to be the best cream ever! Perfect balance and not too sweet!
I made this recipe step by step for my crescent rolls. I make crescent rolls and put this filling in it with nutella. It's absolutely delicious.

Halved the recipe and still have way more than I need to fill a dozen homemade donuts. Followed that recommendation and replaced a bit of vegetable shortening with butter. The end product came out smooth, light, and sweet. This is the first time I have seen a recipe like this when looking for a sweet vanilla filling like my favorite donut places have or in a sweet treat like a Ding Dong or Yodel. I also took some of the cream and added Dutch processed cocoa powder to make some chocolate cream. This recipe is a keeper.
This pastry filling cream was so rich and tasty I have to give it a 12 out of 10🤩🤩🤩
this is perfect for filling cupcakes, donuts , or cakes. I halfed the recipe , followed all instructions and made enough to fill my round cake layers (3)
This is a super easy recipe and tastes great, but it makes ALOT, 1/2 the recipe filled 24 cupcakes and didn't event make a dent.

I made my first fillable donuts . I don't care for fruit filled but lover the soft white cream. I came across this recipe and decided this might be the one. I did change some things based on other reviews. I halved the 1/2 directions and it worked out great. I did use shortening and the butter. My only issue was the grainy syrup. The syrup might have gotten to hot. Having an induction cooktop I thought it would be easier but it was still a little grainy. It still tasted awesome and will be used for my pastries, donuts and whoopie pies. Thanks for a great recipe.

I have been looking for this recipe for it feels like decades! Thanks! It is just perfect for my Saturday morning doughnuts. Hubby doesn't like the bavarian creme filling nor any of the custards. This is the one he likes best.

I’ve been searching for the perfect filling for Whoopie pies after my favorite bakery closed. After years of trying so many different recipes, this is the one! I’m so happy I found it. It sounds like it will be disgusting based on all the oils and shortening, but it comes together and tastes like magic. .
